correctness.rationale: The standard-Euclidean stable-set model is isometric to an alternating-fence order polytope. Slicing at a coordinate facet separates the path; slicing at an edge facet gives a factor of sqrt(2) and two independent truncated paths. The exact recursion A_r'(t)=A_{r-1}(1-t) yields the stated trigonometric generating function. Its nearest pole at pi/2 and next pole at -3pi/2 give a uniform Cauchy remainder O(pi^{-r}), establishing fixed-index and diverging-from-both-ends limits. The two area-sum identities follow from divergence at the origin and at the all-half point. Independent exact-rational checks across dimensions 2 through 9 verify individual facets by alternating-permutation adjacency counts, with numerical checks at dimension 40; these finite checks are only corroboration.

value.rationale: Ordinary Euclidean facet area is a natural full boundary invariant of a standard and widely studied family. All 2n-1 labelled measures are computed exactly with no facet enumeration, and a uniform trigonometric singularity analysis classifies fixed-distance endpoint profiles and the bulk profile. The limiting coordinate areas are pi/2, pi^2/4 and 2 times volume in the first, second and bulk positions, whereas the corresponding edge facets have different constants pi/sqrt(2), sqrt(2)(pi^2/4-pi/2) and sqrt(2). This persistent boundary layer is not recoverable from the common total-area-to-volume ratio, and is useful for local metric comparisons.
